approvedBy: SPECULATIVE — not yet reviewed by Twycross Conservation Education Rangers

core.learnedLine: Bonobos share their food to keep everyone calm.

core.prompt: Stand where your grown-up can see the bonobos behind you. Reach one hand out slow and gentle, the way a bonobo greets a friend. Hold me so I'm in it too.

deep.learnedLine: Bonobos can walk on two legs like me.

core.learnedLine: A big gorilla with a silver back is the one in charge.

core.prompt: Find the biggest gorilla you can see. Stand tall and still like a calm silverback, and let your grown-up take the photo.

core.learnedLine: Gorillas build a fresh leafy nest to sleep in every night.

deep.prompt: Look at a gorilla's hands. Photograph just your own hand held up flat, fingers together, the way a gorilla rests its hand on the grass.

deep.learnedLine: Every gorilla has its own nose print, like my fingerprint.

core.learnedLine: Gibbons have the longest arms of any ape.

core.prompt: Stand where your grown-up can see the gibbons behind you. Now reach both arms up as wide as you can — gibbons have the longest arms of any ape. Hold me up so I'm in it too.

core.learnedLine: Gibbons sing together as a family in the morning.

deep.prompt: Rest me on the fence rail on my own, facing the gibbons, and take a photo of just me looking out at them.

deep.learnedLine: Gibbons swing arm over arm, faster than a person can run.

core.learnedLine: Amur leopards are the rarest big cats in the world.

core.prompt: Crouch down low and slow like a leopard on the hunt, then look up for the photo. Keep me tucked under your arm like a cub.

deep.learnedLine: A leopard's spots are called rosettes, like little flowers.

core.learnedLine: A snow leopard's tail is nearly as long as its whole body.

core.prompt: Get close to the glass and photograph the leopard's spots up close — the thick grey fur and the dark rosettes.

deep.learnedLine: Snow leopards wrap their long tail around themselves to keep warm.

core.learnedLine: One meerkat always stands up on guard to keep the others safe.

core.prompt: Stand up tall and straight like a meerkat on lookout, hands by your sides, chin up. Hold that pose for the photo.

deep.learnedLine: Meerkats take turns being the guard so everyone gets to eat.

core.learnedLine: A giraffe's tongue is longer than my whole arm.

core.prompt: Photograph just the giraffe's coat — the brown patches with the pale lines between them. Every giraffe's pattern is different.

deep.learnedLine: Giraffes only need to sleep for a few minutes at a time.

core.learnedLine: Penguins can't fly in the air but they fly through the water.

core.prompt: Waddle from side to side like a penguin, then stop and smile for the photo with the pool behind you.

deep.learnedLine: Each penguin knows its own chick by the sound of its call.

audio.bonobo_r1: You found the bonobos. Good spotting. Let's watch them together for a moment.
audio.bonobo_l1: Look for a bonobo sitting close to another one. They like to stay near their friends.
audio.bonobo_l1_nv: If they're resting in the shade, that's alright. They keep cool under the leaves when it's warm.
audio.bonobo_f1: Bonobos share their food with each other, even when there isn't much. Sharing keeps everyone calm.
audio.bonobo_e1: Bonobos have gentle ears. Let's be as quiet as we can. Whisper a little hello to them.
audio.bonobo_e1_s: Lovely and quiet. They feel safe when we stay calm and soft.
audio.bonobo_yn1: Can you see a baby bonobo holding on tight?
audio.bonobo_yn1_y: You spotted a little one. Babies hold on to mum all day long.
audio.bonobo_yn1_n: No baby out right now. They're often tucked in close with mum.
audio.bonobo_p1: Time for a photo with the bonobos.
audio.bonobo_b1: You watched the bonobos so kindly and so quietly. Here is your bonobo pin.
audio.bonobo_d1: Here's something else. Bonobos can walk on two legs, just like you, when their hands are full.
audio.bonobo_d2: Find the sign near here that asks us to stay quiet. Say quiet when you spot it.
audio.gorilla_r1: You found the gorillas. Let's stand calmly and watch the family.
audio.gorilla_l1: Look for the biggest gorilla with a silver back. That one is the leader.
audio.gorilla_l1_nv: If the big one is out of sight, watch the little ones playing instead.
audio.gorilla_f1: The big gorilla with a silver back is the one in charge of the whole family.
audio.gorilla_e1: Gorillas like a peaceful space. Let's keep our voices soft and gentle for them.
audio.gorilla_e1_s: Nice and calm. A quiet visitor is a kind visitor.
audio.gorilla_p1: Time for a photo with the gorillas.
audio.gorilla_f2: Every night a gorilla builds a fresh nest out of leaves and branches to sleep in.
audio.gorilla_b1: You watched the gorillas so calmly. Here is your gorilla pin.
audio.gorilla_d1: Let's look at a gorilla's hands up close.
audio.gorilla_d2: Here's a secret. Every gorilla has its own nose print, just like your fingerprint.
audio.gibbon_r1: You found the gibbons. Listen out, they might be singing.
audio.gibbon_f1: Gibbons have the longest arms of any ape, longer than their whole body.
audio.gibbon_p1: Time for a photo with the gibbons.
audio.gibbon_yn1: Can you hear the gibbons calling to each other?
audio.gibbon_yn1_y: You heard them. That's how a gibbon family talks across the trees.
audio.gibbon_yn1_n: All quiet for now. They call most in the early morning.
audio.gibbon_f2: A gibbon family sings together in the morning to say this is our home.
audio.gibbon_b1: You listened to the gibbons so well. Here is your gibbon pin.
audio.gibbon_d1: Let's take a picture of just me watching the gibbons.
audio.gibbon_d2: Gibbons swing arm over arm through the trees, faster than a person can run.
audio.amur_r1: You found the leopard. Look slowly, they are very good at hiding.
audio.amur_f1: Amur leopards are the rarest big cats in the whole world. You are very lucky to see one.
audio.amur_e1: Out here we can be a bit bigger. Let's do our best leopard roar together, nice and loud.
audio.amur_e1_s: What a roar. A leopard would be proud of that.
audio.amur_sh1: Find the sign that talks about the leopard's spots. Say spots when you see it.
audio.amur_b1: You tracked the leopard so carefully. Here is your leopard pin.
audio.amur_d1: A leopard's spots are called rosettes, because each one looks like a little flower.
audio.amur_d2_y: Yes they do. Leopards are brilliant climbers and even nap up in the branches.
audio.amur_d2_n: They really do climb. Leopards are some of the best climbers of all the big cats.
audio.snow_r1: You found the snow leopard. They come from cold, high mountains far away.
audio.snow_l1: Look for that long, thick tail. It's nearly as long as the whole cat.
audio.snow_l1_nv: If the leopard is resting out of sight, watch for it up on the high rocks.
audio.snow_f1: A snow leopard's tail is nearly as long as its whole body, and very thick.
audio.snow_p1: Time for a close-up photo of the snow leopard.
audio.snow_sh1: Find the sign that tells us how tall the mountains are. Say tall when you spot it.
audio.snow_b1: You spotted the snow leopard so well. Here is your mountain pin.
audio.snow_d1: In the cold, a snow leopard wraps its long tail around itself like a scarf.
audio.meerkat_r1: You found the meerkats. Watch closely, they are always busy.
audio.meerkat_f1: One meerkat always stands up on guard to keep the whole family safe.
audio.meerkat_c1: A meerkat on guard is doing an important job. Is it one, digging a hole? Two, watching for danger? Or three, going to sleep? Say one, two or three.
audio.meerkat_c1_c: That's it, number two. The guard watches for danger while the others dig.
audio.meerkat_c1_w: The guard is actually watching for danger, keeping everyone safe.
audio.meerkat_e1: Meerkats scratch and tap in the sand. Give me three claps like a busy meerkat.
audio.meerkat_e1_s: Three claps, brilliant. Just like a meerkat digging away.
audio.meerkat_b1: You watched the lookout so well. Here is your lookout pin.
audio.meerkat_d1: The meerkats take turns being the guard, so everyone gets a chance to eat.
audio.giraffe_r1: You found the giraffes. Look all the way up to see their heads.
audio.giraffe_l1: Look for how a giraffe spreads its front legs wide to reach down for a drink.
audio.giraffe_l1_nv: If none are drinking, watch how they use that long neck to reach the high leaves.
audio.giraffe_f1: A giraffe's tongue is longer than your whole arm, and it's blue-grey to keep it from burning in the sun.
audio.giraffe_c1: How does a giraffe reach the tastiest leaves? Is it one, stretching its long neck up high? Or two, digging down low? Say one or two.
audio.giraffe_c1_c: Yes, number one. That long neck reaches the leaves no one else can.
audio.giraffe_c1_w: It reaches up high with that long neck to the leaves no one else can get.
audio.giraffe_p1: Time for a photo of the giraffe's coat.
audio.giraffe_b1: You looked all the way up. Here is your giraffe pin.
audio.giraffe_d1: Giraffes only sleep a few minutes at a time, often standing right up.
audio.penguin_r1: You found the penguins. Watch them waddle and then dive.
audio.penguin_f1: Penguins can't fly in the air, but they fly through the water using their flippers.
audio.penguin_yn1: Can you see a penguin swimming underwater?
audio.penguin_yn1_y: You spotted a swimmer. Underwater is where a penguin is fastest.
audio.penguin_yn1_n: None in the water yet. Keep watching, one might dive in soon.
audio.penguin_e1: Penguins slap the water with their flippers. Give me two claps like a splashing penguin.
audio.penguin_e1_s: Two claps, wonderful. Splash splash, just like a penguin.
audio.penguin_sh1: Find the sign that tells us what penguins eat. Say fish when you spot it.
audio.penguin_b1: You watched the penguins splash about so well. Here is your penguin pin.
audio.penguin_d1: In a big noisy group, each penguin still knows its own chick just by its call.
